mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% in the current month reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-FEDFUNDS regimes (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.4% in a month following a negative monthly GDP growth reading, it indicates accelerating inflation, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 80% of such triggered months, SPX 20-day returns are positive (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 10,000 suggests strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 10 such months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO above 2% following a sharp drop in RSAFS signals a supply-side recovery that reduces production costs and increases capacity utilization, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During 15 such events, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST rises by more than 15% in a month, it reflects a surge in industrial activity that anticipates stronger corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In 40% of such months, 60-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in UNRATE below 5% indicates weaker wage growth, which reduces the present value of future labor income and can depress equity risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During cooling regimes, 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative (p > 0.2 over 12 months).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months, it suggests a prolonged easing stance that lowers real interest rates and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: In 50 such episodes, 5-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both INDPRO and GDPC1 by at least 1% in the same quarter indicates a dual supply shock, which raises uncertainty and compresses equities, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During 8 such quarters, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.15).
